text:
anna_security: Heads-up — planning an RBAC change for the keystore service next Tuesday 03:00 UTC. Main asks: how do we gate KMS decrypt permission during the canary so we don't break mTLS handshakes in eu-west?

raj_kms: Good call. We need a staged grant: canary role with decrypt-only on the test keystore ARN, then promote. If we flip decrypt for prod instantly, clients will see 403 -> handshake fail.

lee_ops: +1. Can we use a short TTL temporary role and a traffic-sliced rollout? i.e., adjust authz scope only for canary pods behind the canary traffic tag.

anna_security: That's the idea. Also need audit logging requirements — security wants full decrypt attempts logged to the central audit pipeline for a 48h window during rollout. Any perf concerns?

sasha_prodsec: We should sample at 100% for the canary subset, 10% for baseline. Make sure logs include cert_fingerprint, request_id, source_region. We need to correlate with ingress TLS handshake traces.

lee_ops: FYI we saw a previous KMS deny cause this stacktrace in proxy:
```
2024-11-08T12:01:02Z proxy ERROR handshake failed: decrypt denied, err=KMSAccessDenied
stack: net/http -> tls -> proxy/keystore
request_id=abcd-1234
```
If we don't log decrypt attempts, diagnosing will be painful.

raj_kms: Can enable detailed audit for the target key via KMS key policy + CloudAudit logs. We can push a dedicated sink to the secure-audit project. Need OK from infra to increase sink retention for 7 days.

anna_security: Is there a safe fallback during deny spikes? i.e., if KMS returns denies, can proxies gracefully fallback to a lower-tier cert chain or route to another region?

lee_ops: We have a fallback model: if decrypt fails, proxy will attempt fallback-keystore in secondary region (ap-south). But that requires network egress allowed and the cert chain to be compatible. We should validate cert path in preflight.

sasha_prodsec: Add to the preflight checklist: run path validation tool across cert variants + verify ALPN + TLS1.3 enforcement. If fallback-keystore differs in cipher list, clients might fail.

anna_security: I'm adding a small preflight job. Example command for local validation:
```
./cert-checker --keystore s3://keystore-canary --regions eu-west,ap-south --verify-alpn h2 --min-tls 1.3 --report /tmp/cert-report.json
```
Share outputs here before the window.

lee_ops: Also include a smoke test hitting internal endpoints with 512B and 8KB payloads to surface batching/KV cache issues.

raj_kms: Regarding RBAC changes: proposed policy snippet for canary role: 
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"], "Resource": ["arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456:key/canary-key"] },
    { "Effect": "Deny",  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"], "Resource": ["arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456:key/prod-key"], "Condition": {"StringNotEquals": {"aws:PrincipalTag/role": "keystore-canary"}} }
  ]
}
```
That's explicit: canary role sees canary-key decrypt, prod-key denied unless principal has tag. We can iterate.

sasha_prodsec: We also need to ensure audit events include the principal tag and calling principal ARN. Otherwise we can't map which instance attempted the decrypt.

anna_security: Good. On incident response side — if handshake failures spike >1% of baseline in eu-west we abort and roll back RBAC change. Can oncall-bot watch and alert?

oncall-bot: alert-configured: monitor=keystore.handshake_failure_rate; threshold=0.01; window=5m; notify=@eng-oncall,@eng-security; runbook=https://redwood.internal/runbooks/keystore-rotation

lee_ops: I'll stub a quick canary: schedule 10% traffic to canary set for 30m, with a mid-run manual checkpoint. If OK, bump to 30% for 1h.

raj_kms: One more thing — KMS metrics (DecryptErrors) are per-key and delayed ~60s. Use both KMS metrics and proxy-side handshake logs for fast detection.

sasha_prodsec: For TLS hardening, don't change cipher suites during this operation. Keep current ciphers and min TLS version pinned. Any config edits separate from RBAC should happen in a distinct rollout.

anna_security: Agreed. Action items:
- raj_kms: prepare canary key policy & sink (due TOMORROW EOD)
- lee_ops: create preflight job + smoke tests (due TOMORROW EOD)
- sasha_prodsec: audit fields & sampling config (due TOMORROW EOD)
- anna_security: coordinate rollout calendar + update runbook (I'll create PR)

lee_ops: ping me once you have the preflight report, I'll try the fallback validation.

raj_kms: I'll post the key policy draft here when ready.

sasha_prodsec: Also adding a short eval: run the synthetic client that enforces SNI variations and early_data toggles — had a weird edge-case before where 0-RTT attempted replays caused proxy to prefer non-canonical cert.

anna_security: Thanks all. If people are free, quick sync in 20 to walk through the preflight script.

lee_ops: +1, joining.

raj_kms: joining.

sasha_prodsec: joining.

anna_security: meeting link: https://meet.redwood.internal/keystore-rotation-preview

lee_ops: tiny nit — include a log grep snippet we can run in prod to count decrypt denies:
```
# count decrypt denies in last 10m
kubectl logs -l app=proxy -n prod --since=10m | grep -c "KMSAccessDenied"
```

sasha_prodsec: perfect. Also add an ELK saved query for request_id correlation.

anna_security: End of thread for now. I'll post the PR + timeline.
